question_en:
I am organizing materials for a film preservation showcase. Please answer the following questions:

1. Which film does the poster correspond to? Provide the film title and year.
2. What other titles does this film have? In which year did it receive federal funding from the National Film Preservation Foundation, and which institution was responsible for its preservation? Where do the existing film materials originate, in which year was the film restoration completed, and what screening formats does the preserving institution list?
3. Locate the official annual report for that funding year. In the section of the report that lists films preserved over the years, grouped by preserving institution (including the first page of this section), how many separate images are there in total? How many of these images contain no human figures whatsoever? List the annual report page numbers printed at the bottom of all qualifying images. Portraits are also counted as human figures.

Response Format: Answer in numbered points (1)–(3). For question 1, provide the film title and year in text. For question 2, present the requested information in a two-column table with headers "Item" and "Answer". For question 3, provide the two counts and all matching page numbers in text.
answer:
(1) Film Title: Broken Barriers; Year: 1919.

(2)

| Item | Answer |
| --- | --- |
| Alternative Title | Khavah |
| Federal Funding Year | 2017 |
| Preserving Institution | National Center for Jewish Film (NCJF) |
| Source of Existing Film Materials | The only surviving film materials, donated by Sharon Josepho, the great-granddaughter of producer Leopold Kehlmann |
| Restoration Year | 2020 |
| Screening Formats | DCP, Pro-res, Blu-ray, DVD |

(3) There are 8 separate images in total; 2 of them contain no human figures whatsoever. The annual report page numbers printed at the bottom are 30 and 33.

# Detailed Simulated Search Trajectory · 8-3-A01

## Step 01 · Read visible identity clues on the poster

**Action**: Observe the current input image; first transcribe the film title, credits, and production information; example query: "Broken Barriers" "Zion Films" 1919.

**Evidence Observation**: The lower part of the poster shows readable text: BROKEN BARRIERS, Jules Burnstein, Sholom Aleichem, Chas. E. Davenport, and Zion Films; the upper part features four human figures. The poster does not directly give the year of preservation funding or the restoration year; these cannot be inferred from its period appearance.

**Evidence Links**:

https://catalog.afi.com/Film/17325-BROKEN-BARRIERS

**Result of this step**: Use Broken Barriers as the search key to first confirm the film's identity.

## Step 02 · Verify against the AFI Catalog of Feature Films

**Action**: Cross-check the entry with the same title in the AFI catalog to verify whether the year and production credits on the poster match.

**Evidence Observation**: The preserved AFI entry lists Broken Barriers as a 1919 film; the director and production information cross-verify with the credits on the poster. This confirms the original release year, not the later preservation project timeline.

**Evidence Links**:

https://catalog.afi.com/Film/17325-BROKEN-BARRIERS

**Result of this step**: Confirm Broken Barriers (1919).

## Step 03 · Trace the film into the federal preservation grant list

**Action**: Example query: site:filmpreservation.org "Broken Barriers" grant; cross-reference with the 2017 list of funded films.

**Evidence Observation**: The 2017 Federal Grant Winners list Broken Barriers under the National Center for Jewish Film. Linking the film title with the responsible institution provides a more certain determination of the required year than searching only for the same term in the foundation's annual report.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/preserved-films/2017-federal-grant-winners

**Result of this step**: The shared year for the annual report and the preservation project is 2017; the executing institution is NCJF.

## Step 04 · Supplementarily check alternative titles and the material donation chain

**Action**: Read the paragraph about this film in the 2017 funding announcement; record item by item the alternative title, the donor, and their relationship.

**Evidence Observation**: The announcement uses Khavah as the alternative title for this film; the existing materials were donated by Sharon Josepho, the great-granddaughter of producer Leopold Kehlmann. The 57 films and 36 institutions mentioned in the news refer to the total volume of the entire funding round, not the total number of images for this question.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/blog/2017/6/13/57-films-to-be-saved-through-the-nfpf-s-2017-preservation-grants

**Result of this step**: Obtain Khavah and the donation source; avoid mixing the totals from the entire funding round into the image count.

## Step 05 · Confirm restoration and screening formats on the preserving institution's page

**Action**: Read the NCJF page for Broken Barriers (Khavah); separately record the original film identity and the restoration version description.

**Evidence Observation**: The NCJF preservation entry confirms the only surviving film materials, the 2020 restoration, and four screening formats: DCP, Pro-res, Blu-ray, and DVD. The funding occurred in 2017, while the restoration was completed in 2020; these two dates answer different fields.

**Evidence Links**:

https://jewishfilm.org/Catalogue/films/Broken-Barriers.html

**Result of this step**: Sources are secured for all fields in Question 2: alternative title, year, institution, source of materials, restoration, and formats.

## Step 06 · Determine the annual report section and stopping boundary

**Action**: Open the preserved official 2017 annual report; scan page by page starting from the first page of the "Films Preserved through the NFPF" section, stopping before the Financial Statements.

**Evidence Observation**: This section is grouped by preserving institution; the printed page numbers at the bottom range from 10–39, corresponding to PDF reader pages 7–21. The uncaptioned portrait on the section's first page still counts as a separate image and must not be omitted due to the lack of a caption; body text, page numbers, logos, and color blocks are not counted as separate images.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/userfiles/image/PDFs/nfpf_ar2017.pdf

**Result of this step**: Establish the complete set of 8 separate images, including the section's first page.

## Step 07 · Image-by-image verification · Uncaptioned section-opening image

**Action**: Compare this separate image with the layout of its spread; check whether the full image contains real people, portraits, or other depictions of human figures.

**Evidence Observation**: Member p07-img11; PDF page 7 / printed bottom page 10. A frontal portrait occupies the main part of the image; portraits also count as human figures.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/userfiles/image/PDFs/nfpf_ar2017.pdf#page=7

**Result of this step**: Exclude: human figures present.

## Step 08 · Image-by-image verification · The Heath Hen

**Evidence Observation**: Member p09-img12; PDF page 9 / printed bottom page 15. A man wearing a hat holds a bird outdoors; human figures are clearly present.

## Step 12 · Image-by-image verification · Laserimage

**Action**: Compare this separate image with the layout of its spread; check whether the full image contains real people, portraits, or other depictions of human figures.

**Evidence Observation**: Member p17-img16; PDF page 17 / printed bottom page 30. Only abstract red and blue light forms appear; no human figures are present.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/userfiles/image/PDFs/nfpf_ar2017.pdf#page=17

**Result of this step**: Retained as having no human figures.

## Step 13 · Image-by-image verification · Tomb

**Action**: Compare this separate image with the layout of its spread; check whether the full image contains real people, portraits, or other depictions of human figures.

**Evidence Observation**: Member p18-img17; PDF page 18 / printed bottom page 33. Only fallen leaves and ground vegetation appear; no human figures are present.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/userfiles/image/PDFs/nfpf_ar2017.pdf#page=18

**Action**: Compare this separate image with the layout of its spread; check whether the full image contains real people, portraits, or other depictions of human figures.

**Evidence Observation**: Member p21-img18; PDF page 21 / printed bottom page 39. Multiple pedestrians are visible in the urban street scene; the cinema marquee does not change this determination.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/userfiles/image/PDFs/nfpf_ar2017.pdf#page=21

**Result of this step**: Exclude: human figures present.

## Step 15 · Re-verify the page numbers for the two matches with no human figures

**Action**: Return from the images to the bottom of their respective pages, rather than copying the PDF reader page numbers.

**Evidence Observation**: Laserimage corresponds to printed page 30 (PDF 17); Tomb corresponds to printed page 33 (PDF 18). Page 21, which contains a clipped portrait, and page 10, the section's first page, serve as counterexamples.

**Evidence Links**:

https://www.filmpreservation.org/userfiles/image/PDFs/nfpf_ar2017.pdf#page=17

https://www.filmpreservation.org/userfiles/image/PDFs/nfpf_ar2017.pdf#page=18

**Result of this step**: Output page numbers 30 and 33; 2 matches out of 8 images.

## Step 16 · Re-verify closure of the full set and sources of fields

**Action**: Align the item-by-item checklist with each requirement in the current question; recalculate the candidate count and the match count separately; then verify identifiers, page numbers, names, and answer format.

**Evidence Observation**: The closed set for this task is 8; the screening result is 2.
